the question of whether and how a post-structuralist metalanguage can support and extend the linguistic resources of students as writers.
the development of a metalanguage adequate for the analysis of students’ achievement in post- structuralism and English.

the introduction of post-structuralism into a senior school English course has the potential to provide a powerful metalanguage for the development of students’ linguistic achievement in English, as evidenced by their capacity to handle the demands for voicing in their writing.

the introduction of a metalanguage for voicing in post-structuralist theory and English has the potential to enhance students’ capacities for reflexive engagement with the texts of others and for their own literary and linguistic achievement.

the metalanguage provided to students in this course is adequate to the achievement of their linguistic goals.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the metalanguage of systemic functional linguistics is a powerful tool in supporting teachers and learners to develop their capacity for reflexivity.
the metalanguage of systemic functional linguistics is a powerful means of supporting students’ development of sophisticated voicing and of helping them to reflect critically on their own writing.
